YZ19/82 calls the Lang torsor missing without separating the existing Picard Lang theorem already planned by YZ17/52 at GS.0; /79 and /110 likewise need reconciliation with YZ17/38's bundle/Picard inputs. Confirmed omitted sufficient smoothness hypothesis. Item 217 quotes only d≥3g−2+N, whereas Proposition 5.5(1), p.467, supplies smooth pure-dimensional M_d under d≥2g'−1+N=4g−3+rho+N; this stronger bound is used in pp.490–491 when fundamental classes induce endomorphisms of the constant sheaf via duality. Retain both smoothness/duality and smallness contracts and proper support. Qualify the finding's numerical aside: the difference is g−1+rho, which equals zero for an unramified cover of a genus-one curve. The defect is the missing general hypothesis, not a universally strict gap or a proof that every smaller-degree M_d is singular.

Confirmed sign inconsistency by direct trivialization calculation. Lemma A.5, p.518, maps (L,tau_eta,tau_x) to tau_x composed with tau_eta^(−1). For L=O_X(x), the local generator is varpi^(−1), so tau_x relative to the natural generic inclusion is multiplication by varpi: the displayed map sends O_X(x) to varpi, not varpi^(−1). Sections 6.2.3–4 use t→div(t) and O_X(−E), consistent with this calculation and inconsistent with /163's copied normalization. Correct that normalization or invert the entire equivalence consistently. Quadratic eta is inversion invariant, but the divisor/line-bundle API still requires a single sign convention.

Confirmed unstated strengthening. Proposition 6.2(3), p.495, states commutativity of (6.4), and item 127 records only that. Proposition 7.3, pp.508–509, additionally uses finiteness of g_d over A_d^diamond and that the square is Cartesian there. Over a,b nonzero the matrix sections are all nonzero, so divisor splittings give a finite root-addition problem and the defining nonvanishing conditions are automatic; properness then yields finiteness. State this open restriction explicitly and do not claim the full diagram Cartesian over the zero-section boundary, where Definition 6.1's degree-dependent condition selects a branch.

Confirmed missing regularization convention. Item 136 presents the weighted sum uniformly for all orbital classes. Vanishing grouped tails does not imply absolute finiteness of the ungrouped weighted set.

Confirmed that the asserted four-term Picard-stack exactness needs replacement, with a qualification to the proposed fix. A trivialization of L^(−1)⊗sigma*L belongs to the homotopy kernel of 1−sigma; at L=O it can be rescaled by any unit. Over a geometric base the scalar automorphisms of L cannot remove that factor, whereas descent from Pic_X imposes the norm/cocycle constraint. Thus the sheaf exact sequence on p.524 does not directly give the naive Picard-stack exactness copied by /174 from p.525. Page 481 needs the lift with its specified root-norm trivialization. Factor through torsors under K=ker(root norm), retaining homotopy fibres and descent/obstruction data. Do not replace it by ordinary zero-ended short exact sequences asserting naive injectivity: in an étale double cover the nontrivial quadratic line already pulls back to O.
